name: Why the fish stalls earned less in May
subject: economics
question: cause
brief: Your economics sheet gives four weeks of May figures from the fish-stall cooperative at Nabapara Old Market. Rohu arrivals rose by twelve per cent and retail prices held steady, yet the stalls' net earnings fell from 620 rupees a stall-day in April to 540 in May. The bell rings in ten minutes and, as recorder, you must write down what squeezed the stalls' margin.

claims.name: Hotter mornings forced the stalls to buy far more ice to keep the fish from spoiling
Unsold stock had to be cleared at a discount because the market's cold room was out of use
Wholesale prices at the dawn landing rose sharply and squeezed the stalls

evidence.name: Cooperative ice-chute chits rose from 45 rupees to 85 rupees per stall-day between April and May
Shade thermometer logs in the market averaged 39 degrees Celsius at noon over the four May weeks
Sales after eleven o'clock averaged 30 rupees a kilogram below the board price at opening
The market superintendent's book records the overnight cold room shut for twelve days awaiting a valve
The dawn landing sheet shows wholesale rates four per cent lower than in April
The brass and iron pan weights were stamped by the inspectors in April

limitations.name: The cooperative's table covers only its eight licensed stalls and leaves out the basket sellers by the gate
Fish taken home by stall families at closing time is counted in with the discounted sales
Two senior stalls own insulated boxes whose ice use is pooled into the cooperative total

note: Nabapara Old Market (loc_old_market) is from INDIA_WORLD_BIBLE.md; the figures are invented. The ice outlay explains 40 of the 80 rupees lost a stall-day, so a second cause is needed, and the markdowns supply it; that is why two claims are defensible. The wholesale claim is contradicted by the landing sheet. The pan weights are beside the point.
